title: Emily Wilde's Encyclopaedia of Faeries
author: Heather Fawcett
summary: A prickly Cambridge scholar travels to a snowbound northern village to research the hidden folk for her great reference work. Her charming academic rival turns up uninvited, and the village's faeries are less harmless than they look.
readIf: you want a snowy, bookish fantasy with a socially awkward heroine and a romance that creeps up on her.
skipIf: you want a lot of action, since much of the book is field notes, village life and careful folklore.

pairings.reason: A fairy-tale forest that is genuinely menacing, a prickly heroine and a slow-growing bond with a difficult man.
A lighter, more modern take on academic rivals turned allies, without any of the folklore.
Cold, folklore-rich and full of household spirits, but more solemn and rooted in medieval Russia.
